conventions.convention: Flat spacetime has signature (−,+,+,+), a chosen future cone, and inertial coordinates x⁰=ct. Proper-time velocities satisfy η(U,U)=−c²; future timelike velocities have U⁰>0.
The prescribed external field is an alternating covariant two-tensor, with Fᵃ_b=ηᵃᶜF_cb. The physical SI dictionary is F₀ᵢ=−Eᵢ/c and Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖBₖ; no singular self-field is evaluated on the worldline.
The LL lemma requires F∈C² on an open region, α∈ℝ and τₑ≥0. Its formula Π_U=Id+U⊗U♭/c² is defined for every U; its orthogonal-projection interpretation applies on the normalized timelike shell.

The residual estimate uses inertial-component Euclidean norms and induced operator norms, C³ curves near a common closed interval, and five bounds uniform in ε. The separate stability comparison uses explicitly scaled coordinate ℓ¹ norms, existing solutions in a common compact region, and identical initial states.

The physical LAD coefficient is τₑ=q²/(6πε₀mc³)>0 for m>0 and q≠0, with ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹. LAD is an adopted effective equation for at least C³ curves; approximation validity is separate from equation-level deductions.

The Abraham–Lorentz example is a separate scalar ODE on all real coordinate times, with a nonnegative nonzero smooth pulse supported in [0,T], m>0, τₑ>0, and a(+∞)=0. Its integral to infinity is a finite-support truncation.

Shrinking-body literature results assume a specified scaling family and do not establish an unrestricted fixed-charge point limit. The qualification agrees with [Gralla–Harte–Wald, §II and §§V–VI](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0905.2391).

load_bearing.statement: For an oriented, time-oriented four-dimensional affine Minkowski space, a fixed inertial chart, c>0, an open region O, a C² alternating covariant two-tensor F, α∈ℝ and τₑ≥0, the explicitly defined system x′=U, U′=f₀+τₑΠ_UB has a unique local solution through every (x₀,U₀)∈O×S⁺ on an open interval about 0. Along that interval η(U,U)=−c² and U remains future directed. No global existence is claimed.

For the stated flat charged-body model with prescribed C² external two-form, m>0, q≠0 and τₑ=q²/(6πε₀mc³)>0, adopt aᵃ=f₀ᵃ+τₑ(daᵃ/dτ−η(a,a)Uᵃ/c²) for sufficiently regular curves, at least C³. No existence, uniqueness, stability or empirical claim is part of this postulate.

For the stated C³ normalized LAD family on a common compact interval, fixed C² field and uniform bounds |αε|≤A, ‖F‖op≤M, ‖ΠUε‖op≤P, ‖δε‖≤C₀ε and ‖δ̇ε‖≤C₁ε, the LL acceleration residual is at most P(C₁+AMC₀)ε² throughout that interval. Separately, the two specified second-order phase fields, Lipschitz on a common compact region with constant at most L and differing there by at most Cτₑ², have existing same-initial-state solutions remaining there within Cτₑ²Te^(LT) on [0,T].
